ut_sprocket_rocks.blurb: Sprocket Rocks is a small outcrop in the juniper hills west of Cedar City, one of the crags grouped as West Cedar Crags. Most of the 18 climbs are bolted sport lines, with a handful of trad routes and two boulder problems, V2 and V3. Grades start around 5.6 and reach into the low 5.12s, but the bulk sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers working on moderate-to-hard face and crack climbing more than first-timers. The walls are short, with nothing needing a long rope, and the setting is open and sunny. Ticks are reported to be heavy, so check yourself and any dog after a day out.

ut_isolation_wall.blurb: Isolation Wall is a compact sport crag tucked into a small alcove close to The Membrane in American Fork Canyon, on limestone. The 18 routes run from an easy 5.7 up through 5.12, and the middle-to-hard grades dominate: mostly 5.10 to 5.12 with only a couple of 5.9s. The two sides of the alcove differ: the east wall is a bit overhanging and harder, while the west wall is lower-angled, polished smooth by water and more about balance. The east side picks up sun from around midday to mid-afternoon, and the crag overall is shaded later in the day, which makes it a handy summer evening choice when its neighbour is baking.

vt_butchers_island.blurb: Butchers Island is one of four sectors of the Butchers' Crags in the Lamoille River valley of northern Vermont. It is a shady little cliff with an easy walk in and a modest set of worthwhile routes, mostly traditional lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, plus a couple of bolted routes, a top-rope and a good number of boulder problems. Bouldering makes up half of the 18 climbs, ranging from VB up to one hard outlier, with most problems V0 to V5. The shade makes it a pleasant pick on warm days, and the low-grade trad climbs make it approachable for those building gear skills.

va_thews_boulder.blurb: Thews Boulder is a single large block in the Middle Boneyard, part of the big boulderfield on the mountainside at Grayson Highlands State Park in southwest Virginia. The block stands about 12 to 13 feet tall and leans slightly out. Its left side is blank and topped by a thin sloping rim that makes finishing tricky, the middle follows a faint arete on pinches and crimps, and the back offers sloping holds. All 18 problems are bouldering, spread from V0 to V8 with a weight toward the harder end, V6 and V7 especially. Bring plenty of pads; this is more of a project boulder for strong climbers than a beginner stop.

va_12_2_boulder.blurb: The 12.2 Boulder is a roadside block beside the Blue Ridge Parkway in the Charlottesville area, at roughly 2,900 feet, so close to the pavement that it is easy to combine with other stops along the Parkway. It holds 18 boulder problems and is a high-end venue: the lines run from V3 to V10, but most are V7 to V9, so it suits strong boulderers more than newcomers. The climbing is on the greenstone typical of the northern end of the Parkway, which has sharp edges and can feel slick in muggy weather. Pads should not be left stashed along the roadside.

va_gumby.blurb: Gumby is a large boulder in the main area of The Forest, the biggest cluster of greenstone boulders along the Blue Ridge Parkway near Charlottesville. Its faces are slightly overhanging, and it carries 18 problems that cover nearly the full range, from a VB warm-up through a broad middle of V2 to V6 up to a single V10. That makes it one of the friendlier boulders for a mixed group, since each climber can find something at their level. The woods sit noticeably cooler than the town below, which helps on hot days.

va_the_vault.blurb: The Vault is a sport crag in the Mile Two section of Guest River Gorge in southwest Virginia, set in a big amphitheater of sandstone. Its 18 routes are all bolted and aimed at experienced climbers: nothing easy, starting around 5.10 and mostly in the 5.12 and 5.13 range, with a couple at 5.14. Several of the hard lines stay dry in heavy rain. With the trees bare, the amphitheater sees sun in the morning and shade later on, while the remainder of the wall does the reverse, and it is rated as a strong cold-weather crag on sunny days.
